entities.name: Torchitorio IV of Cagliari
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Barisone II Torchitorio IV de Serra, reigning as Judike of Arborea from 1185 until his death in 1217, momentarily unified two of Sardinia's four independent giudicati by also becoming Judike of Cagliari from 1214 to 1217. His reign was defined by the complex political landscape of 13th-century Sardinia, a strategic island coveted by rival maritime powers, particularly the Republics of Pisa and Genoa, and by the papacy seeking to assert its suzerainty. Torchitorio's efforts to maintain Sardinian autonomy amidst these external pressures and internal dynastic struggles illuminate the island's precarious position as a pawn in larger Mediterranean power games.

Barisone II ascended to the Judicature of Arborea following the death of his father, Hugh I. His marriage to Agnes of Massa, daughter of William I of Cagliari (Salusio IV), strategically positioned him to inherit the Judicature of Cagliari. Upon William I's death in 1214, Barisone seized control of Cagliari, assuming the regnal name Torchitorio IV, thereby consolidating significant power in central and southern Sardinia. This unification, however, was short-lived and fiercely contested by Lamberto Visconti, a Pisan noble who had married Elena of Gallura and sought to expand Pisan influence. The ensuing conflict saw Pisan forces actively intervening, leading to a period of intense warfare and political instability across the island.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Torchitorio IV's brief unification of two Sardinian giudicati and subsequent conflicts with Pisa profoundly shaped Sardinia's political trajectory, leading to increased foreign domination rather than lasting independence. His reign exemplifies the island's persistent struggle against powerful external forces during the Medieval period.
